claims.title: Sogdiana settled and under Achaemenid rule
claims.summary: The Zeravshan valley of Sogdiana, centred on Maracanda (Samarkand), is settled and passes under the Achaemenid Persian Empire; Bukhara grows as a Silk Road trade and crafts centre.

sources.label: Sogdiana — Central Asia, Silk Road, Persian Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1000bce-sogdiana-settled-and-under-achaemenid-rule, claim TL:UZB:event:1000bce:sogdiana-settled-and-under-achaemenid-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alexander the Great conquers Sogdiana
claims.summary: Alexander the Great captures Maracanda (Samarkand) and advances to the Jaxartes, overcoming two years of fierce Sogdian resistance under Spitamenes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-329bce-alexander-the-great-conquers-sogdiana, claim TL:UZB:event:329bce:alexander-the-great-conquers-sogdiana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alexander marries Roxana of Bactria
claims.summary: To cement his conquest, Alexander marries Roxana, daughter of the Bactrian chieftain Oxyartes, symbolising the union of Macedonian and Central Asian peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-327bce-alexander-marries-roxana-of-bactria, claim TL:UZB:event:327bce:alexander-marries-roxana-of-bactria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sogdians dominate Silk Road trade
claims.summary: Sogdian merchants from Samarkand and Bukhara become the leading caravan traders of the Silk Road, their language a lingua franca of Inner Asian commerce and culture.

sources.label: Sogdiana — Central Asia, Silk Road, Persian Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-500-sogdians-dominate-silk-road-trade, claim TL:UZB:event:500:sogdians-dominate-silk-road-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab conquest of Bukhara and Samarkand
claims.summary: The Umayyad commander Qutaybah ibn Muslim takes Bukhara and Samarkand and annexes Transoxiana, beginning the Islamisation of the region beyond the Oxus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-712-arab-conquest-of-bukhara-and-samarkand, claim TL:UZB:event:712:arab-conquest-of-bukhara-and-samarkand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Talas
claims.summary: Abbasid Arab forces defeat the army of Tang China at the Battle of Talas, confirming Islam's hold on Central Asia and, by tradition, spreading papermaking westward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-751-battle-of-talas, claim TL:UZB:event:751:battle-of-talas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Samanid Bukhara, a centre of the Islamic Golden Age
claims.summary: The Persian Samanid dynasty makes Bukhara its capital, a rival to Baghdad whose court fosters Persian literature, science and the refined art and architecture of the Islamic Golden Age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-875-samanid-bukhara-a-centre-of-the-islamic-golden, claim TL:UZB:event:875:samanid-bukhara-a-centre-of-the-islamic-golden, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Imam al-Bukhari and the Sahih
claims.summary: Muhammad al-Bukhari, born in Bukhara, compiles the Sahih, accepted by Sunni Muslims as the most authoritative collection of the Prophet's sayings after the Qur'an.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-810-imam-al-bukhari-and-the-sahih, claim TL:UZB:event:810:imam-al-bukhari-and-the-sahih, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Genghis Khan sacks Bukhara and Samarkand
claims.summary: The Mongol armies of Genghis Khan storm Transoxiana, destroying Bukhara and Samarkand in a devastation from which the oasis cities took generations to recover.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1220-genghis-khan-sacks-bukhara-and-samarkand, claim TL:UZB:event:1220:genghis-khan-sacks-bukhara-and-samarkand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Timur takes power and makes Samarkand his capital
claims.summary: Timur (Tamerlane) seizes control of Transoxiana and makes Samarkand the capital of an empire reaching from Anatolia to India, adorning it as the cultural heart of Central Asia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1370-timur-takes-power-and-makes-samarkand-his, claim TL:UZB:event:1370:timur-takes-power-and-makes-samarkand-his, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bibi-Khanym mosque and Timurid Samarkand
claims.summary: Timur summons artisans from across his conquests to build the monumental Bibi-Khanym mosque and other masterpieces, making Samarkand one of the great cities of the medieval world.

sources.label: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures — World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1399-the-bibi-khanym-mosque-and-timurid-samarkand, claim TL:UZB:event:1399:the-bibi-khanym-mosque-and-timurid-samarkand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ulugh Beg builds his observatory
claims.summary: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg, ruler and astronomer, builds a great observatory at Samarkand and compiles star tables so accurate they were used in Europe two centuries later.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1428-ulugh-beg-builds-his-observatory, claim TL:UZB:event:1428:ulugh-beg-builds-his-observatory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Shaybanid Uzbeks conquer Transoxiana
claims.summary: Muhammad Shaybani Khan leads the Uzbeks south, expelling the last Timurids from Samarkand and Herat and founding the Shaybanid dynasty ruling from Bukhara.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1500-shaybanid-uzbeks-conquer-transoxiana, claim TL:UZB:event:1500:shaybanid-uzbeks-conquer-transoxiana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The khanate of Khiva is founded
claims.summary: A branch of the Shaybanid dynasty establishes the khanate of Khiva in the Khwarezm oasis, one of the three Uzbek states that would endure until the Russian conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1512-the-khanate-of-khiva-is-founded, claim TL:UZB:event:1512:the-khanate-of-khiva-is-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The khanate of Kokand emerges
claims.summary: A third Uzbek state, the khanate of Kokand, rises in the fertile Fergana Valley, completing the trio of khanates of Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1709-the-khanate-of-kokand-emerges, claim TL:UZB:event:1709:the-khanate-of-kokand-emerges, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islamic monuments of Bukhara and Khiva
claims.summary: The khanates raise the madrasas, minarets and palaces that survive in the historic centres of Bukhara and the walled Itchan Kala of Khiva, today UNESCO World Heritage sites.

sources.label: Historic Centre of Bukhara — World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1619-islamic-monuments-of-bukhara-and-khiva, claim TL:UZB:event:1619:islamic-monuments-of-bukhara-and-khiva, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russia takes Tashkent
claims.summary: Russian imperial forces storm Tashkent, beginning the conquest of the Uzbek lands; Samarkand falls in 1868 as the empire pushes into Central Asia.

sources.label: Uzbekistan — The Russian Conquest (Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1865-russia-takes-tashkent, claim TL:UZB:event:1865:russia-takes-tashkent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khanates absorbed into Russian Turkestan
claims.summary: Bukhara (1868) and Khiva (1873) become Russian protectorates and Kokand is annexed in 1876, completing the conquest and the creation of Russian Turkestan.

sources.label: Uzbekistan — The Russian Conquest (Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1876-khanates-absorbed-into-russian-turkestan, claim TL:UZB:event:1876:khanates-absorbed-into-russian-turkestan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Creation of the Uzbek SSR
claims.summary: The Soviet national delimitation of 1924 carves Central Asia into ethnic republics; the Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic is created and becomes a union republic of the USSR in 1925.

sources.label: Uzbekistan — The Russian Conquest (Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1924-creation-of-the-uzbek-ssr, claim TL:UZB:event:1924:creation-of-the-uzbek-ssr, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cotton monoculture and the death of the Aral Sea
claims.summary: Soviet irrigation for cotton diverts the Amu Darya and Syr Darya, and the Aral Sea shrinks drastically from the 1960s — a notorious man-made environmental catastrophe.

sources.label: Desiccation of the Aral Sea
sources.publisher: Seventeen Moments in Soviet History, Michigan State University

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1960-cotton-monoculture-and-the-death-of-the-aral-sea, claim TL:UZB:event:1960:cotton-monoculture-and-the-death-of-the-aral-sea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uzbekistan declares independence
claims.summary: The Supreme Council of the Uzbek SSR declares independence on 31 August 1991; 1 September becomes Independence Day, and a December referendum confirms it with Islam Karimov as first president.

sources.label: Uzbekistan — Countries (U.S. recognition and relations)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-1991-uzbekistan-declares-independence, claim TL:UZB:event:1991:uzbekistan-declares-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Andijan events
claims.summary: Government forces open fire on protesters in the city of Andijan; rights groups estimate that hundreds of civilians were killed, drawing international condemnation of Karimov's rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-2005-the-andijan-events, claim TL:UZB:event:2005:the-andijan-events, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mirziyoyev succeeds Karimov and opens reforms
claims.summary: After Islam Karimov's death, Shavkat Mirziyoyev becomes president and launches a 'New Uzbekistan' programme of economic liberalisation and cautious political opening.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-2016-mirziyoyev-succeeds-karimov-and-opens-reforms, claim TL:UZB:event:2016:mirziyoyev-succeeds-karimov-and-opens-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of systemic forced labour in cotton
claims.summary: After sustained reforms and international monitoring, civil-society groups conclude that Uzbekistan has dismantled the systemic state-imposed forced labour in its cotton harvest.

sources.label: Uzbekistan Ends Systemic Forced Labor, Civil Society Says

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uzbekistan: Heart of the Silk Road — Samarkand, Bukhara and the empire of Timur.", terralore.co/country/UZB/chronicle#ev-2022-end-of-systemic-forced-labour-in-cotton, claim TL:UZB:event:2022:end-of-systemic-forced-labour-in-cotton, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
